info.title: NoResponse API
info.summary: Server-side risk assessment of account creation, login and purchase: a recommendation, polling and signed webhooks.
info.description: Assess an account creation, login or purchase and get back the account's one current risk, poll a pending assessment, page through an account's history, record what you later learned, report usage of the API keys you issue to your accounts, rotate your API key, manage your webhook endpoints, and register hosted endpoints that answer your WorkOS, Auth0 or Supabase sign-up and sign-in hooks. Every response carries X-Request-ID; every error is an RFC 9457 problem document. Keep the API key on your server.

post.summary: Assess identifiers for a signup or gateway decision.
post.description: Assesses one account creation, login or purchase (flow) and answers with the account's one current risk: account.risk.decision is the decision for this flow (allow, step_up, review or block, where block means your block threshold was reached), and detail holds this assessment's own facts. depth sets how long the answer waits for sources: quick waits only for the fast ones (500 ms), full for the whole budget (3000 ms at most); it defaults to full for account_creation and purchase and quick for login. 200 carries complete or partial, 202 carries pending with Location and Retry-After. While the account's first assessment is pending, account is absent: apply your own fallback for that, 429, 503 or a timeout. NoResponse blocks nothing itself; you decide. Requires the assess scope. Idempotency-Key is required and is bound to the body for 24 hours: the same key with the same body replays the latest assessment with Idempotent-Replayed: true and starts no new work; the same key with a different body answers 409 idempotency_key_reused. response_mode defaults to standard; detailed needs the detailed scope.

get.summary: Poll the authoritative assessment of one assessment.
get.description: Returns the highest assessment_version, with the account's current risk. Requires the assess or history scope. While status is pending, or partial with a source still running, the response carries Retry-After; poll no faster than it says. Another workspace's assessment, an unknown or expired assessment and a malformed assessment_id all answer 404 not_found. response_mode=detailed needs the detailed scope.

parameters.name: response_mode
parameters.description: Optional standard or separately authorised detailed customer view; raw is rejected.

delete.description: Deletes one assessment in the environment of your key, with its versions, evidence and outcomes and the identity-graph marks its outcomes set, and scores its account again from what remains. Afterwards the assessment answers 404 and leaves the account's history. The answer names the account and the assessment its current risk now comes from; current_assessment_id is absent when the account has no assessment with a decision left. Requires the history scope. An unknown, expired or already deleted assessment answers 404, so a repeat answers 404; to erase a whole account idempotently, use accounts.delete.

post.summary: Report what was later learned about an assessed account.
post.description: Records what you later learned about an assessed account: confirmed_abuse, account_takeover and chargeback report abuse; false_positive and legitimate withdraw your earlier report; unknown is recorded only. Outcomes are append-only and the latest one wins. Requires the assess scope. Idempotency-Key is required and handled as on POST /v1/assessments: a retry with the same key and body answers the same record with Idempotent-Replayed: true; a different body answers 409. An unknown, expired or foreign assessment answers 404 not_found.

value.notes: Card testing from this account; closed by trust and safety.

post.summary: Page through one account's unexpired assessments.
post.description: History is a POST with account_id in the body so an account identifier stays out of URLs and access logs. Requires the history scope. Read-only and safe to retry. Newest first, each at its latest assessment_version. An account with no assessments answers 200 with empty items. The cursor is opaque and bound to your workspace and the account; a tampered or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor. response_mode=detailed needs the detailed scope.

get.summary: Poll the accounts whose risk changed.
get.description: Your accounts whose risk changed, oldest change first, each as accounts.get answers it. Every page carries next_cursor: pass it back as changed_since to read the changes made after that page; without changed_since the list starts from the oldest change. When nothing changed, items is empty and next_cursor is the cursor you sent, so poll by calling again with the latest next_cursor. An account appears again each time its risk changes, with a higher risk_version; keep the copy with the highest. unenforced=true lists only accounts with a decision other than allow for some flow and no applied enforcement at their current risk_version; such a page can hold fewer than limit items, or none, while later changes exist, so keep polling with next_cursor. Requires the history scope. Read-only and safe to retry. A tampered or foreign cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor.

parameters.name: changed_since
parameters.description: next_cursor from an earlier page, unchanged. Absent, the list starts from the oldest change.

parameters.name: unenforced
parameters.description: true lists only accounts with no applied enforcement at their current risk_version that have a decision other than allow for some flow or a hold no later applied enforcement resolved.

get.summary: Read an account's one current risk.
get.description: An account is the account_id you send with your assessments. Its current risk is the risk of its latest assessment with a decision (status complete or partial), scored as GET /v1/assessments/{assessment_id} scores that assessment, with a decision for each flow; risk.decision is the decision for the flow of that assessment. Every assessment answers with this same account. Every assessment updates its account: once an assessment completes, the account carries its risk. Requires the history scope. Read-only and safe to retry. An account with no unexpired assessment that has a decision answers 404 not_found, and a malformed account_id answers 400 invalid_request.

delete.summary: Erase an account and its history.
delete.description: Erases the account in the environment of your key, for an erasure request from your user: every assessment of it, with its revisions, evidence and outcomes, and the identity-graph marks its outcomes set. An assessment of the account begun before the call is refused or stopped. Afterwards the account and each erased assessment answer 404 and the history is empty. When the call deleted at least one assessment, an account.deleted event goes to your verified webhook endpoints. Requires the history scope. Idempotent and safe to retry: a repeat, or an account with nothing to erase, answers 200 with assessments_deleted 0 and sends no event. The account_id can be assessed again later, as a new account.

get.summary: Page through one account's unexpired assessments.
get.description: The account's history: the same page as POST /v1/assessments/query for this account_id, newest first, each at its latest assessment_version. Requires the history scope. Read-only and safe to retry. An account with no assessments answers 200 with empty items. The cursor is opaque and bound to your workspace and the account; a tampered or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor. response_mode=detailed needs the detailed scope. The account_id travels in the URL; use POST /v1/assessments/query to keep it out of access logs.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged.

parameters.name: response_mode
parameters.description: Optional standard or separately authorised detailed customer view; raw is rejected.

post.summary: Record what you did to an account in your identity provider.
post.description: Records what you did to the account in your identity provider for one flow's decision at one risk_version: the action (or none), the account's state before it, the provider and whether it was applied or failed. It is your action, not an outcome, and it leaves the account's risk unchanged. A record is kept once per account, risk_version, flow and action: the first report answers 201, and a repeat answers 200 with the stored record unchanged, so retries are safe without an Idempotency-Key. An applied report after a failed one replaces the failed record, keeping its id and created_at, and answers 201. A risk_version older than the account's current one is accepted and stored, but only an applied record at the current risk_version takes the account out of listChanged with unenforced=true; a newer one answers 409 risk_version_ahead. An account with no current risk answers 404 not_found. error_code is allowed only with status failed. Requires the history scope.

post.summary: Report requests made with API keys your platform issued.
post.description: Records requests made with API keys your platform issued to your accounts, one event per request: the key's SHA-256 (the issued_credential.sha256 the account's assessment carried), the client IP, the time and optionally the user agent, model and token counts. Most callers use the SDK's usage buffer, which batches events and sends them in the background. Sampling is allowed: sample_rate weights an event's request and token counts. Requires the assess scope. Idempotency-Key is required and handled as on POST /v1/assessments: a retry with the same key and body answers the same record with Idempotent-Replayed: true and counts nothing again; a different body answers 409. A batch holds 1 to 500 events and at most 256 KiB. No raw event is kept: usage is aggregated per key, and IPs, user agents and models are kept only as keyed digests, with the IP's country, for 24 hours. When one key is used from 20 or more IP addresses, or 3 or more countries, within 24 hours, every account whose assessment carried that key gets the shared_api_key reason for 30 days.

post.summary: Rotate the API key that signs the request.
post.description: Mints a new key with the same scopes as the key that signs the request and returns it once. The presented key keeps working for overlap_seconds (default 24 hours, from 60 seconds to 7 days), then answers 401. A key accepts one rotation: rotating again with a key already in its overlap answers 409 key_rotation_in_progress, so rotate with the new key. Rotation is not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer mints another key.

Registers a WorkOS, Auth0 or Supabase integration and returns its hosted endpoint, url, so a sign-up or sign-in is scored with no server of your own. For WorkOS, send the Actions signing secret from the WorkOS dashboard and point the user registration and authentication Actions at url. For Supabase, send the hook secret Supabase generates (v1,whsec_...) and set url as the Before User Created hook's HTTPS endpoint. For Auth0, the answer's secret is the shared secret of the NoResponse Auth0 Action, shown once: store it as an Action secret. hook_points defaults to every hook point the platform has (Supabase has only pre_registration); an event that is not listed is allowed without an assessment. The endpoint waits for the full assessment for at most 2.5 seconds (WorkOS, Supabase) or 4.5 seconds (Auth0), denies only when risk.block is true and allows on any failure. Requires the integrations scope; at most 10 per account. Not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer registers another integration.

get.description: Every integration, oldest first. Listings carry no secrets. Requires the integrations scope.

delete.description: Removes the integration and its secrets; its endpoint answers 404 from then on, so remove the Action from the provider first. Requires the integrations scope. An unknown or already deleted integration answers 404.

post.description: For Auth0, send {} and the answer's secret is the new shared secret, shown once. For WorkOS, regenerate the Actions secret in the WorkOS dashboard and send it as signing_secret; for Supabase, generate a new hook secret in the Supabase dashboard and send it as signing_secret. The replaced secret is still accepted for 24 hours (previous_secret_expires_at). Requires the integrations scope. Not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer rotates again.

get.description: Lists your webhook endpoints in every state, ordered by endpoint_id, with the ids of their signing keys and without secrets. Requires the webhooks scope.

post.description: Registers a webhook endpoint and returns it with its first signing secret, shown only in this answer: store it where your receiver reads it. The URL is https on port 443 or 8443 with a DNS host whose every address is public; it is checked now and on every delivery. The endpoint starts unverified and receives assessment events once it echoes an endpoint.verification challenge, which sendTestEvent sends. You can hold 5 endpoints. Requires the webhooks scope, and response_mode detailed also the detailed scope. Registration is not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer registers a second endpoint, which you can list and delete.

delete.description: Deletes the endpoint and its signing keys. Deliveries still queued for it are dropped. Requires the webhooks scope. An endpoint that is already gone answers 404.

post.description: Issues a new signing key for the endpoint and returns its secret once. Every delivery from now on is signed with it; the key it replaces keeps verifying for 7 days, so your receiver can hold both while it switches. Requires the webhooks scope. Rotation is not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer issues another key, which replaces the first.

post.summary: Send a test event to an endpoint.
post.description: endpoint.verification sends a signed challenge now and answers whether the endpoint echoed it within 5 seconds; an echo verifies the endpoint, including a disabled one. assessment.updated queues one signed event with test: true and a fixed example assessment in the endpoint's response mode, delivered and retried like any other event; the endpoint must be verified. Both use the endpoint's current signing key. Requires the webhooks scope.

Creates an API key in the environment of the key that signs the request, with scopes that key holds itself, and returns its secret once in key. Requires the management scope; the new key may hold it too. A scope the signing key lacks answers 403 workspace_forbidden, and the other environment 404 not_found. An environment holds at most 100 keys that authenticate (409 key_limit_reached). created_by is the signing key's prefix. Not idempotent: a retry after a lost answer creates a second key, which you can list and revoke.

get.description: Lists the keys of the signing key's environment, newest first, at most 200, revoked and expired keys included, without secrets: each key's id, prefix, scopes, status, and who created and revoked it. Requires the management scope. Read-only and safe to retry.

delete.description: Revokes a key of the signing key's environment at once: its next request answers 401. Requires the management scope. A key of the other environment or of another workspace answers 404 not_found. A key cannot revoke itself (409 self_revocation): rotate it with keys.rotate, or revoke it with another management key. Revoking a revoked key changes nothing and answers the key as it was revoked, so a retry is safe.

get.description: Reads the settings of the signing key's environment: retention in days; per flow (account_creation, login, purchase) the step_up, review and block thresholds, the default depth and the admission; and the sources the environment refuses. A flow without thresholds of its own shows account_creation's with inherits_account_creation true. Requires the management scope; the other environment answers 404 not_found. Read-only and safe to retry.

patch.description: Changes only what the body names, in one transaction: retention_days, refused_sources, and per flow step_up, review, block (null turns blocking off), default_depth, admission, hold_seconds, on_expiry, or inherits_account_creation to return login or purchase to account_creation's thresholds. After the change each flow keeps 0 < step_up < review <= 100 and block off or review <= block <= 100; a change that breaks it answers 400 naming the flow. A policy change is one new policy_version with the signing key's prefix as updated_by, and every change is recorded in the workspace's audit log with the key as its actor. Requires the management scope; the other environment answers 404 not_found. A change reaches assessments within a minute.

get.description: Every POST the endpoint received, newest first: the event id and type, which attempt it was, whether it was a replay, delivered or failed, the response code, why it failed and how long it took. Attempts are kept for 30 days, or your retention_days when that is shorter, and are deleted with the assessment they carried. Requires the webhooks scope. Read-only and safe to retry. The cursor is opaque and bound to your workspace and the endpoint; a tampered or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged.

post.description: Queues the event for the endpoint again: the same event id and body it received, with a new NR-Webhook-Timestamp and a signature from the endpoint's current signing key, retried like any other delivery and listed with replay: true. Your receiver deduplicates on the event id. The endpoint must be verified. Requires the webhooks scope. Not idempotent: each call, a retry included, sends the event again.

apiKey.description: Your API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys are opaque, scoped (assess, history, webhooks, integrations, and optionally detailed) and identify one workspace. Rotate with POST /v1/keys/rotate. A missing, malformed, revoked or expired key answers 401; a key without the operation's scope answers 403.

Account.description: Body of the 200 answer to GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}: the one current risk of one of the calling workspace's accounts. It is the risk of the account's latest assessment that has a decision (status complete or partial), by created_at and then assessment_id, scored exactly as GET /v1/assessments/{assessment_id} scores that assessment, plus the account's own reason shared_api_key when a key issued to the account was used from many IP addresses or countries (POST /v1/key_usage/batches). Its assessments are the account's history (GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}/assessments).

id.description: The account_id the workspace sends with its assessments.

decisions_by_flow.description: The decision for each flow: the account's score under that flow's thresholds. A flow the workspace has not set uses its account_creation thresholds, so the flows differ only where it set them. The flow of the current assessment is held while that flow's admission is held and the assessment's investigation has not completed.

assessment_id.description: The assessment the current risk comes from.

updated_at.description: updated_at of that assessment's latest revision.

risk_version.description: The version of the account's current risk. It increases every time the account's current risk or decisions_by_flow changes, and does not decrease. Of two copies of an account, the one with the higher risk_version is newer. account.risk_changed carries the risk_version that its change made.

AccountDecision.description: block when the score reached your block threshold (risk.block of the assessment), otherwise the assessment's recommendation. held only for a flow whose admission is held (settings flows.<flow>.admission), when the account's current assessment was made for that flow and its investigation has not completed (status partial): the final decision arrives as account.risk_changed when the investigation completes, decided by its score, or when the hold's deadline (hold_seconds after the assessment was created) passes first, as the flow's on_expiry action or the decision the evidence so far gives, whichever is stricter. Your application applies it.

AccountDecisionsByFlow.description: The decision for each flow: the account's score under that flow's thresholds. A flow the workspace has not set uses its account_creation thresholds, so the flows differ only where it set them. The flow of the current assessment is held while that flow's admission is held and the assessment's investigation has not completed.

AccountDeleted.description: Terminal for the account's assessments created at or before deleted_at in the receiving endpoint's environment: delete what you hold from them and ignore later-arriving updates of them. deleted_at is no earlier than the creation of any assessment it erased. An assessment created after it belongs to the account assessed again: keep it, even when this event arrives after it.

account_id.description: Your own opaque identifier for the account being checked, scoped to your workspace. Use an id you mint, with no direct identifier (email, phone, name or national id) in it. '|' is accepted so an Auth0 user id such as 'auth0|64abc' passes unchanged; '@', '+', '$' and whitespace are refused by the pattern, as is an exact-shape JWT; a hex digest such as a SHA-256 is allowed, because hashing an internal id is a common pseudonymous scheme. A value such as '07700900123' or 'jane.doe.gmail.com' cannot be told apart from an opaque id. It travels in bodies, and in a URL only as the path segment of GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} and its /assessments. An assessment requested by a provider hook at pre_registration, which has no account yet, carries the server-issued account_id pre: followed by its assessment_id.

assessments_deleted.description: How many assessments the erasure deleted.

deleted_at.description: When the erasure took effect, equal to deleted_at in the DELETE answer.

id.description: The event id, equal to the NR-Webhook-Id header and across redeliveries and every endpoint the event fans out to.

created_at.description: When the event was created. Equal across redeliveries; the signing timestamp header is per delivery.

test.description: Present, and true, only on an event sent by POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test: its data is a fixed example assessment, not one of the workspace's, so a receiver acknowledges it and applies nothing. Real events have no test member.

AccountDeletion.description: Body of the 200 answer to DELETE /v1/accounts/{account_id}: the calling workspace's account was erased in the environment of the calling key. Every assessment of the account went, with its revisions, evidence, outcomes and the identity-graph marks its outcomes set, and an assessment that was still running when the call arrived is stopped. Afterwards GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} and GET /v1/assessments/{assessment_id} of each erased assessment answer 404, and the history page is empty. The call is idempotent: a repeat, or an account with nothing to erase, answers 200 with assessments_deleted 0. The account_id can be assessed again later, as a new account.

assessments_deleted.description: How many assessments this call deleted. 0 when the account had none left, so a repeat answers 0.

deleted_at.description: When the erasure took effect. An assessment of the account begun before this time is refused or stopped.

AccountList.description: Body of the 200 answer to GET /v1/accounts: the calling workspace's accounts whose risk changed after changed_since, in the environment of the calling key, oldest change first. An account is listed when its risk_version advanced and it has a current risk, and each item is the account exactly as GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} answers it. An account appears once per page, at its latest change; when its risk changes again later, it appears again on a later page with the newer risk_version. next_cursor is always present: pass it back as changed_since to read the changes made after this page.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor after the last change this page read, bound to the workspace and the environment of the calling key. Pass it back unchanged as changed_since. It is present on every page, the last one included: when nothing changed after changed_since it is the cursor that was sent, so a poller keeps calling with the latest next_cursor. A tampered or foreign cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor. Consumers do not parse it.

score.description: 0 (safe) to 100 (risky), as risk.score of the assessment.

decision.description: The decision for the flow of the assessment this account is served with: on GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}, the flow of the current assessment; inside an assessment, that assessment's flow.

reasons.description: Every reason that fired: risk-raising reasons first, then neutral, then risk-lowering, each strongest impact band first and then by code. The policy's numeric weights are kept private, so a reason carries only its direction and impact band.

AccountRiskChanged.description: The account's decision for at least one flow changed. account is the account as GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} answers it for the revision that made the change: its new score, decision, reasons and decisions_by_flow, and the assessment the risk comes from. previous_decisions_by_flow are the decisions it replaced, so account.decisions_by_flow differs from them for at least one flow. On the account's first decision, previous_decisions_by_flow is allow for every flow. Events of one account are not ordered: account.risk_version orders them, so keep the account with the highest risk_version and ignore an event whose account is older than the one held.

previous_decisions_by_flow.description: The decision for each flow before the change, as last announced.

id.description: The event id, equal to the NR-Webhook-Id header and across redeliveries and every endpoint the event fans out to.

created_at.description: When the event was created. Equal across redeliveries; the signing timestamp header is per delivery.

test.description: Present, and true, only on an event sent by POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test: its data is a fixed example assessment, not one of the workspace's, so a receiver acknowledges it and applies nothing. Real events have no test member.

Admission.description: immediate (the default): an assessment of this flow is decided from the evidence its answer has, and later evidence may change the decision. held: while the account's current assessment of this flow has not completed, the account's decision for the flow is held, and the final decision arrives as account.risk_changed when the investigation completes or hold_seconds pass, whichever is first. Each flow has its own admission.

Assessment.description: One assessment, as POST /v1/assessments, GET /v1/assessments/{assessment_id} and the assessment.updated webhook return it. account is the account's one current risk: its score, the decision for this assessment's flow, the reasons and the decision for each flow. detail holds this assessment's own facts. status says whether the assessment is final (complete), usable with a source still running (partial) or not yet usable (pending). While the account's first assessment is pending, account is absent; wait for the webhook or poll the assessment. Keep the highest detail.assessment_version.

id.description: This assessment's id, equal to detail.assessment_id.

status.description: This assessment's status, equal to detail.status. While it is pending, account carries the risk of the account's previous decided assessment, or is absent.

flow.description: The flow the request named. account.risk.decision is the decision for it. An assessment made before flows existed reports account_creation.

depth.description: The depth the assessment was served at: the request's, or its flow's default. An assessment made before depths existed reports full.

account.description: The account's one current risk when this assessment was served, decided for this assessment's flow: the body GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} would answer, with risk.decision equal to decisions_by_flow for flow, which is held while this assessment's flow is held and its investigation has not completed. Absent only while the account has no assessment with a decision (its first assessment is still pending); a webhook or GET of the decided assessment then carries it.

detail.description: This assessment's own facts: its score, recommendation, signals, coverage and timing.

AssessmentDeletion.description: Body of the 200 answer to DELETE /v1/assessments/{assessment_id}: one of the calling workspace's assessments was deleted, with its versions, evidence, outcomes and the identity-graph marks its outcomes set. Afterwards GET /v1/assessments/{assessment_id} answers 404 and the assessment leaves the account's history. The account is scored again from what remains: account.current_assessment_id names the assessment GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} now serves its risk from, and is absent when the account has no assessment with a decision left. Deleting an assessment that is already gone answers 404.

id.description: The account_id of the deleted assessment.

current_assessment_id.description: The assessment the account's current risk now comes from. Absent when the account has no assessment with a decision left, and GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} then answers 404.

AssessmentDetail.description: One assessment's own facts: its score and recommendation, the signals behind them, the lanes still running and its timing. risk here is this assessment's own score; the account's current risk is the account member of the assessment. risk and recommendation are present for complete and partial; assessment_url is present for pending.

assessment_id.description: Opaque, server-assigned assessment id: 'asm_' and a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID. Unique within the workspace; another workspace's assessment id answers 404.

account_id.description: Your own opaque identifier for the account being checked, scoped to your workspace. Use an id you mint, with no direct identifier (email, phone, name or national id) in it. '|' is accepted so an Auth0 user id such as 'auth0|64abc' passes unchanged; '@', '+', '$' and whitespace are refused by the pattern, as is an exact-shape JWT; a hex digest such as a SHA-256 is allowed, because hashing an internal id is a common pseudonymous scheme. A value such as '07700900123' or 'jane.doe.gmail.com' cannot be told apart from an opaque id. It travels in bodies, and in a URL only as the path segment of GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} and its /assessments. An assessment requested by a provider hook at pre_registration, which has no account yet, carries the server-issued account_id pre: followed by its assessment_id.

request_id.description: An optional provider correlation id, echoed back. It is not an idempotency key. Refuses an exact-shape JWT or a bare 40, 64 or 128 character hex digest; a UUID is accepted.

signals.description: Detailed view only (response_mode=detailed, which needs the detailed scope): a standard answer omits signals[], and a detailed one always carries it, possibly empty. The body does not name its mode, so that rule is the serving gate's; the schema states the half it can: an answer with risk.details is a detailed view and carries signals[]. At most one signal per (type, source_id, identifier).

incomplete_sources.description: The lanes that did not settle, each listed once with a reason; lanes, not sources. In a detailed view a lane is listed exactly when one of its signals did not settle; a standard view carries no signals to match.

policy_version.description: Version of the hand-authored heuristic policy that produced the recommendation, for example 'risk-2026-10.7'. A workspace threshold override adds a +t<N> suffix, e.g. 'risk-2026-10.7+t3'.

policy_basis.description: Labels the v0 policy as hand-authored and not statistically validated.

assessment_version.description: Monotonic revision of this assessment. 1 on the synchronous answer; each material change while the assessment is served (an async continuation settling a source, a change of recommendation, confidence or status) increments it. Expiry does not increment it: an expired assessment is gone, not revised, and the expiry webhook carries the last served version.

created_at.description: When the assessment was created. Fixed for the life of the assessment: every revision carries the same created_at.

expires_at.description: After this instant the assessment is no longer served: GET /v1/assessments/{assessment_id} answers 404 and it leaves the account history. It is created_at plus your retention period at creation (default and maximum 365 days) and is fixed per record: a later revision keeps it, and a new assessment for the same account starts its own clock. If you later shorten retention, the effective expiry becomes created_at plus the shorter of the two periods.

assessment_url.description: Server-relative path of the authoritative assessment, GET /v1/assessments/{assessment_id}.

auth_context.description: The identity fields of the auth context the assessment was made with, echoed for the workspace's own correlation: the request's auth_context, or the one a hosted provider hook (POST /hooks/{integration_id}) built, with transport provider_hook and its hook_point. Present exactly when the request carried an auth_context, and the same on every revision of the assessment. Values are as the request or the hook sent them; tokens, timestamps, roles and scopes are not echoed, and the echo does not change the score.

AssessmentDetailAuthContext.description: The identity fields of the auth context the assessment was made with, echoed for the workspace's own correlation: the request's auth_context, or the one a hosted provider hook (POST /hooks/{integration_id}) built, with transport provider_hook and its hook_point. Present exactly when the request carried an auth_context, and the same on every revision of the assessment. Values are as the request or the hook sent them; tokens, timestamps, roles and scopes are not echoed, and the echo does not change the score.

provider.description: The provider slug the context named.

subject.description: The subject the context named; absent when it named none (a pre_registration hook).

session_id.description: The session identifier the context named, when it named one.

organization_id.description: The organization identifier the context named, when it named one.

verified.description: The verified flag the context carried. A provider_hook context is always false.

transport.description: Where the context was derived: backend (also when the request named no transport), browser, or provider_hook for a hosted provider hook.

hook_point.description: The provider event a provider_hook context was sent for; absent for any other transport.

deadline_ms.description: The budget the server applied to the synchronous answer.

elapsed_ms.description: Server time from HTTP ingress to this revision of the assessment.

AssessmentExpired.description: Terminal. Nothing to fetch; the consumer deletes its state for assessment_id.

assessment_id.description: Opaque, server-assigned assessment id: 'asm_' and a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID. Unique within the workspace; another workspace's assessment id answers 404.

account_id.description: Your own opaque identifier for the account being checked, scoped to your workspace. Use an id you mint, with no direct identifier (email, phone, name or national id) in it. '|' is accepted so an Auth0 user id such as 'auth0|64abc' passes unchanged; '@', '+', '$' and whitespace are refused by the pattern, as is an exact-shape JWT; a hex digest such as a SHA-256 is allowed, because hashing an internal id is a common pseudonymous scheme. A value such as '07700900123' or 'jane.doe.gmail.com' cannot be told apart from an opaque id. It travels in bodies, and in a URL only as the path segment of GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} and its /assessments. An assessment requested by a provider hook at pre_registration, which has no account yet, carries the server-issued account_id pre: followed by its assessment_id.

assessment_version.description: The last served version: expiry is not a revision.

AssessmentList.description: Body of the 200 answer to POST /v1/assessments/query: one page of the calling workspace's unexpired assessments for one account, newest first, each at its latest assessment_version, as its detail; the account's current risk is GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}. Every item's account_id equals the page's. An assessment past its expires_at is not listed. next_cursor is present only when another page exists.

account_id.description: Your own opaque identifier for the account being checked, scoped to your workspace. Use an id you mint, with no direct identifier (email, phone, name or national id) in it. '|' is accepted so an Auth0 user id such as 'auth0|64abc' passes unchanged; '@', '+', '$' and whitespace are refused by the pattern, as is an exact-shape JWT; a hex digest such as a SHA-256 is allowed, because hashing an internal id is a common pseudonymous scheme. A value such as '07700900123' or 'jane.doe.gmail.com' cannot be told apart from an opaque id. It travels in bodies, and in a URL only as the path segment of GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} and its /assessments. An assessment requested by a provider hook at pre_registration, which has no account yet, carries the server-issued account_id pre: followed by its assessment_id.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, bound to your workspace and the account_id it was issued for. Pass it back unchanged in the next query; a tampered, foreign or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor.

retention_days.description: Your current retention period, so a consumer knows how far back history reaches. Every item expires no later than its created_at plus this many days.

AssessmentOutcome.description: The 202 answer of POST /v1/assessments/{assessment_id}/outcomes. A replay with the same Idempotency-Key and body answers the same record.

id.description: Opaque, server-assigned id of one recorded outcome: 'out_' and a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID. Unique within the workspace.

assessment_id.description: Opaque, server-assigned assessment id: 'asm_' and a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID. Unique within the workspace; another workspace's assessment id answers 404.

received_at.description: When NoResponse first recorded the outcome.

AssessmentOutcomeRequest.description: POST /v1/assessments/{assessment_id}/outcomes body: what the provider later learned about the account it assessed. The assessment is named by the path and the workspace by the API key, so neither is a body member. Idempotency-Key is required and binds the body as it does on POST /v1/assessments.

observed_at.description: When the provider observed the outcome. Defaults to when NoResponse received it.

external_ref.description: Your own opaque reference for the outcome, such as a case or ticket id. Stored as given and not interpreted; keep direct identifiers out of it.

notes.description: Free text for your own records, at most 500 characters. Stored only; it is left out of scoring and answers. Keep personal data out of it. Control characters other than tab and line breaks are refused.
notes.example: Chargeback filed two days after account creation.

AssessmentQuery.description: POST /v1/assessments/query body. account_id travels in the body rather than the URL path so a provider value that turns out to hold personal data is not written to access logs, proxies or browser history. Read-only: no Idempotency-Key. An account with no unexpired assessments answers 200 with empty items.

account_id.description: Your own opaque identifier for the account being checked, scoped to your workspace. Use an id you mint, with no direct identifier (email, phone, name or national id) in it. '|' is accepted so an Auth0 user id such as 'auth0|64abc' passes unchanged; '@', '+', '$' and whitespace are refused by the pattern, as is an exact-shape JWT; a hex digest such as a SHA-256 is allowed, because hashing an internal id is a common pseudonymous scheme. An assessment requested by a provider hook at pre_registration, which has no account yet, carries the server-issued account_id pre: followed by its assessment_id.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged. Opaque, MAC'd and bound to the workspace and account_id.

response_mode.description: standard returns the consolidated risk response; detailed adds merged provider-neutral facts when the key has detailed scope. There is no raw mode.

AssessmentRequest.description: POST /v1/assessments body. At least one of email, username or phone is required; name and ip only refine an assessment. No field carries a password, hash, token or breach value, and unknown members are refused. The email local part is kept as received and only the domain is lower-cased; the username is compared case-insensitively; the phone is strict E.164 and is assessed asynchronously. The whole body is capped at 32768 bytes. client_context holds bounded hints from the client of the user; auth_context holds normalised claims from a session your backend has verified. Raw tokens are refused.

account_id.description: Your own opaque identifier for the account being checked, scoped to your workspace. Use an id you mint, with no direct identifier (email, phone, name or national id) in it. '|' is accepted so an Auth0 user id such as 'auth0|64abc' passes unchanged; '@', '+', '$' and whitespace are refused by the pattern, as is an exact-shape JWT; a hex digest such as a SHA-256 is allowed, because hashing an internal id is a common pseudonymous scheme.
